messages:
sara_sales: Quick one — ACME (enterprise) sent a SIG/CAIQ focused on IAM. They want concrete evidence for: SSO/SAML metadata, MFA enforcement for console/interactive logins, RBAC role mappings (IdP groups -> Redwood roles), least-privilege on service accounts, and a sample audit log extract. Can security/eng confirm what we can provide and ETA?

emily_security: We can provide SAML metadata, SCIM provisioning docs, a redacted audit export, an RBAC mapping table, and an attestation that MFA is required for interactive sessions (they usually accept IdP screenshots). Need to know which deployment mode they're evaluating (Hosted vs Dedicated/Private) since some enforcement points differ. Also confirm if they need SOC2 evidence signed or just screenshots + export.

dan_engineering: For RBAC — we support role definitions and group mapping. Typical roles: admin, dev, deployer, read-only. We can map multiple IdP groups to a single role and vice versa. Example mapping config (redacted):
```yaml
roles:
  - name: admin
    permissions: [*]
  - name: deployer
    permissions: [deploy:create, deploy:read]
group_to_role:
  - group: acme-eng
    role: deployer
  - group: acme-admins
    role: admin
```
Service accounts: we issue short-lived OIDC tokens for machine clients and recommend using dedicated service principals with minimal scopes. API keys are long-lived by default — recommend rotating and scoping.

oliver_cs: I'll coordinate the POC test with ACME. They can provide an Okta metadata XML and a test user. Need to know if we require SCIM/just SAML for the POC. Also they asked whether MFA is enforced on API calls made via the console (they expect interactive sessions to require MFA).

sara_sales: They said MFA for console login and SSO is mandatory. They don't require MFA for service-to-service tokens but want rotation policy and short TTLs. They also requested a sample RBAC export and a redacted audit log showing a create/delete event.

emily_security: Confirming: MFA enforced at the IdP level for SSO — we rely on the customer's IdP policy. For Hosted customers we enforce session checks and validate SAML assertions; for Dedicated/Private, enforcement is inside their VPC and we can document where controls apply. For API keys we don't force MFA, instead we provide guidance to use short-lived OIDC tokens and ephemeral creds + KMS. We'll produce:
- SAML SP metadata (XML)
- SCIM + provisioning guide (PDF)
- RBAC table CSV with example mappings
- Redacted audit export (CSV) showing user events
- Attestation PDF stating MFA enforced for interactive sessions (requires legal sign-off)
Links: https://confluence.redwood.example.com/security/iam-evidence (will upload artifacts)

dan_engineering: I can generate a minimal SAML metadata file and a sample audit CSV. ETA: EOD tomorrow for initial bundle. For the POC, we just need the customer's IdP metadata and a test acct. We support SAML v2.0 and SCIM v2.0.

sara_sales: Perfect. ACME also asked whether group renames break mappings — can you confirm behavior?

emily_security: Group name changes will break group->role mapping if the IdP sends the group name as the key. We recommend mapping using persistent group IDs where possible, or using SCIM for authoritative membership. We'll note this in the RBAC doc.

jane_legal: I can review and sign the attestation. Please route the drafted PDF to legal@sales.redwood.example.com. We typically need a 48-hour review window.

deploy-bot: Deploy check: artifact upload path created at /confluence/security/iam-evidence (attachments pending).

oliver_cs: I'll ask ACME to share Okta metadata + a test user. Scheduling: they suggested next Tue 10:00 PT. Does that work for eng/security for a 30-min SAML handshake?

\dan_engineering: Tue 10:00 PT works for me. I'll bring the sample metadata and a quick test plan: create test user -> SSO login -> check role mapping -> trigger an audited action.

emily_security: Works for security as well. We'll prepare screenshots and the attestation draft.

sara_sales: Thanks team — I'll confirm with ACME and update the thread. If anything else comes up (e.g., they ask for MFA screenshots from our Okta org) note we can't expose our org but can provide equivalent screenshots and redacted proof. :thumbsup:
